Use these commands to take an entry out of your reports, or to bring it back after a mistake. The undo command takes out the last entry that you added on this device.

:::caution
A removed entry leaves your reports and searches. The entry stays in the database, and the restore command brings it back. Read the [backups guide](/gournal/docs/guides/data-safety-and-backups/) for backups.
:::

## CLI

### gournal undo

Remove the last entry that you added on this device. Restore it later by id.

```text
gournal undo
```

### gournal restore

Bring back a removed entry.

```text
gournal restore <id>
```

#### Arguments

| Argument | Required | Description |
|----------|----------|-------------|
| `<id>` | yes | The full id or the last 8 characters of the removed entry. |

## MCP tool: delete_entry

Remove an entry. The entry stays in the database, so you can restore it with the CLI command `gournal restore <id>`.

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | `string` | yes | Full id or the last 8 characters of the entry. |

### Output

This tool returns structured output. The shape is the [Entry result](/gournal/docs/reference/output-shapes/#entry-result).

## Examples

### CLI

#### gournal undo

Remove the last entry that you added on this device. The command prints the id that restores it.

```console
$ gournal add "Draft the release notes for 2.4" -t docs
✓ Entry added! (1QGS52KG)

$ gournal undo
✓ Removed: Draft the release notes for 2.4 (restore with gournal restore 1QGS52KG)
```

#### gournal restore

Bring back an entry that you removed. Pass the short id that `undo` printed.

```console
$ gournal restore 1QGS52KG
✓ Restored: Draft the release notes for 2.4
```

### MCP

Delete an entry. The entry stays in the database. The text result tells you the command that restores it.

```json
{
  "id": "1QGS52KG"
}
```

The text result:

```text
Entry 1QGS52KG deleted: Draft the release notes for 2.4
restore with gournal restore 1QGS52KG
```

The structured result has the same shape as the `add_entry` result. The `deletedAt` field holds the time of the deletion.

```json
{
  "entry": {
    "id": "01M7G81WDZ12AE5Q5X1QGS52KG",
    "createdAt": "2026-11-15T18:38:29.311Z",
    "updatedAt": "2026-11-15T18:39:12.024Z",
    "deletedAt": "2026-11-15T18:39:12.024Z",
    "deviceId": "01M7G81PASZ2E8T209BWDT235N",
    "summary": "Draft the release notes for 2.4",
    "details": null,
    "kind": "done",
    "status": null,
    "resolvedAt": null,
    "resolvedByEntryId": null,
    "project": "billing-api",
    "repo": null,
    "branch": "main",
    "source": "cli",
    "agent": null,
    "tags": [
      "docs"
    ],
    "refs": []
  },
  "notes": []
}
```
